18 odd days → 18/7 = 2 weeks and 4 odd days.

then, 19 July 2015 will be Wednesday + 4 = Sunday.

= 14(March) + 30(Apr) + 31(May) + 30(June) + 19(July) = 124 days.

= 124 days → 124/7 = 17 weeks and 5 odd days.

So, **17 March 2015** will be Sunday - 5 = Tuesday.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: If 10 October 2003 was a Friday, then what was the day of the week on 8 October 2015?
questions.solution:
Given: **10 October 2003** was Friday.

Now,

2003 to 2015 = 12 Years (9 Ordinary Years and 3 Leap Years).

And, In 12 Years = 3 Leap years and 9 Ordinary Years.

So, 3 Leap Years have 6 odd days,

And, 9 Ordinary Years have 9 odd days.

Total odd days = 6 + 9 = 15.

15 odd days → 15/7 = 2 weeks and 1 odd day.

Then, 10 October 2015 will be Friday + 1 = Saturday.

Now, the number of days between 10 October 2015 to 8 October 2015

= 2 days.

So, **8 October 2015** will be Saturday - 2 = Thursday.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: There are 160 multiple choice questions in a test. 4 marks are allotted for a correct answer and 1 mark is deducted for a wrong answer or un-attempted question from the total score of correct answers. If a candidate scored 400 marks in the test, how many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If all questions were answered correctly, the total score would be 160 × 4 = 640 marks.

The total marks lost from the maximum possible score = 640 − 400 = 240 marks.

Marks lost per incorrect or un-attempted question = 4 (for correct) + 1 (penalty) = 5 marks.

Number of incorrect or un-attempted questions = 240 ÷ 5 = 48.

Number of correctly answered questions = 160 − 48 = 112.

**∴ The correct answer is 112 questions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total questions = 160

Marks for a correct answer = +4

Marks for a wrong or un-attempted answer = −1

Total score obtained = 400 marks

**Method Used: Alligation**

⇒ If all 160 questions are correct, total score = 160 × 4 = +640

⇒ If all 160 questions are wrong or un-attempted, total score = 160 × (−1) = −160

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49a278fd89da73ac61af134bb9bb1e5ef4f35840483429dc4ad797f6ad27ef87.png] 

⇒ The ratio of Correct to Wrong questions = 560 : 240 = 7 : 3

⇒ Total ratio parts = 7 + 3 = 10 parts

⇒ 10 parts = 160 questions

⇒ 1 part = 160 ÷ 10 = 16 questions

⇒ Correct questions = 7 parts = 7 × 16 = 112 questions

**∴ The correct answer is 112 questions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation Approach

Let the number of correct answers be x. Then the incorrect or un-attempted answers will be (160 − x). The equation is formulated as 4x − 1(160 − x) = 400.

Rule of Alligation

It is a quick cross-multiplication visual method used to find the ratio in which two components of different values are combined to produce a specific average overall value.

Penalty Mark Evaluation

In negative marking exams, each mistake causes a total loss equal to the correct mark plus the penalty mark. For example, in this case, the total loss per error is 4 + 1 = 5 marks.

a dynasty that appeared in eastern India
a dynasty that appeared in Puri
a dynasty that united eastern India and Burma

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A dynasty that appeared in eastern India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dynasty Overview:**

 
 
• Period: Ruled from the 8th to 12th centuries.
 
• Founder: Gopala established the dynasty around the 8th century.
 
• Regions: Primarily Bengal and parts of Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Religious and Cultural Contributions:**
 
 
• Buddhism: The Palas were prominent patrons of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• Educational Institutions: Founded and supported renowned Buddhist universities like Nalanda and Vikramashila.
 
 
 
• **Key Rulers:**
 
 
• Dharma Pala (circa 770–810 CE): Consolidated and expanded the empire, strengthening its influence.
 
• Devapala (circa 810–850 CE): Furthered the empire's reach and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Decline and Legacy:**
 
 
• The empire declined due to invasions by the Cholas and the rise of new regional powers, including the Senas.
 
• The Palas are remembered for their significant contributions to art, architecture, and the promotion of Buddhist learning and culture in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: On 7 November 2022, the Supreme Court of India upheld the reservations for the weaker sections (EWS). Which of the following amendments brought this reservation in the first place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**103rd Amendment of the Constitution.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Introduction of EWS Reservation:**

 
 
• Objective: Provides 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in educational institutions and government jobs.
 
• Criteria: Applies to individuals not covered by SC, ST, or OBC reservations, based on economic status.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 15: Allows for the provision of reservation in educational institutions for EWS.
 
• Article 16: Permits reservation in government employment for EWS.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility:**
 
 
• Income Limit: Individuals with annual income below ₹8 lakh or possessing less than 5 acres of land are eligible.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Expansion: Increases the scope of affirmative action by including economically disadvantaged individuals who are not otherwise covered by existing reservation policies.
